answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a sonnet as the anchor of the cost.
